RXV2-0.9.543-esc-catch-hardening: Scorpion ESC editor hardening (coffee-break review): preparing the receiver now forgets a stale 'flight controller holds the settings' flag (firmware), and the page only trusts that flag once the receiver has actually restarted since you pressed the button; a single silent flight-controller answer no longer flashes 'no link' (the FC reboots after Release); MSP settings polls are strictly one at a time so a silent FC cannot pile requests up on the receiver; the idle readiness probe can no longer run twice after the page is re-shown.
RXV2-0.9.542-esc-page-one-text: Scorpion ESC editor: the three text areas on the start screen are now ONE patch of text that says what to do first and why second (Blades off, press the button, restart the battery… — then the 10-second rule and the telemetry-freeze note). The deaf-ESC button reads 'Prepare the receiver to read the ESC on reboot…'; the note under the button is gone. Page-only change.
RXV2-0.9.541-esc-read-honest-button: Scorpion ESC editor: the start screen now explains the 10-second rule (a Scorpion only listens for 10 s after power-up) and checks, safely through the ESC's live telemetry, whether a read can work. The button says what will work: 'Read the ESC' when the flight controller already holds the settings or the ESC has just powered up, 'Restart the battery to read the ESC' when the ESC is deaf (it arms the receiver's catcher first, then waits for your battery restart), greyed only when there is no flight-controller link or the receiver is busy catching. Honest end-of-catch messages (transmitter on at power-up, nothing published). Release now shows the battery button straight away. Catch status API gains result/poweron and ?got=0.
RXV2-0.9.540-save-toast-visible: Scorpion ESC editor: the 'Saved - read back from the ESC and confirmed' message now actually appears above the Save button (it was written but never displayed).
RXV2-0.9.539-install-watchdog: Update safety: the receiver no longer goes deaf if a WiFi download stalls. A download that stops for 25 s is abandoned (firmware unchanged), a task watchdog reboots the receiver if anything else wedges during an install, and the events log now records each download's size and time. Handshake timeout trimmed to 20 s.
RXV2-0.9.538-esc-catcher-safe-wifi-first: Scorpion ESC editor: Save now confirms right above the button ("Saved - read back from the ESC and confirmed"). Boot catcher made safe: a stale arm survives software reboots but a transmitter heard at power-up cancels it (never freezes ESC telemetry at the field); Cancel button on the battery card. Updates prefer the receiver's own WiFi: if it is still joining, the app waits (up to 45 s) instead of pushing over Bluetooth - unless the home network is out of range.
RXV2-0.9.537-esc-release-by-effect: Scorpion ESC editor: Release now judges itself by effect - it retries the reset write and waits for the ESC's telemetry to come back (up to 20 s), reporting the live voltage - a lost acknowledgement no longer reads as a failed release. Idle status reads "Press Read the ESC to start".
RXV2-0.9.536-esc-boot-catcher: Scorpion ESC editor: the receiver now catches the ESC by itself. A Scorpion only listens for a programmer in its first 10 s after power-up, so when the editor sees no answer it arms the receiver; pull the battery, wait 5 s, plug in, and the receiver asks the flight controller for the ESC settings during those first seconds - the phone only has to reconnect. First live read + verified write on the Goblin 770 (Tribunus II 14S-200A).
RXV2-0.9.404-auto-fly: NEW: Automatic fly mode (Receiver settings, ON by default) - for everyone who forgets Fly now. When the model is armed and the sticks have been moving for 5 seconds, the receiver switches WiFi and Bluetooth off by itself so nothing interferes with the radio link; everything returns automatically after landing. Needs the arming channel set.
RXV2-0.9.403-add-picker: Switches page: 'Add a switch action' now first asks WHAT the switch should do (a drop-down of all the functions), then creates the row with that choice ready.
RXV2-0.9.402-drag-handles: Switches page polish: the blue zone's round ends can now be DRAGGED with a finger to set the range (numbers follow along, snapped to 5 µs), and the live channel marker is a slim red line (green inside the zone).
RXV2-0.9.401-range-bars: Switches page: each row now shows the configurator-style range bar - the blue zone is where the function is ON, and a LIVE dot shows the channel's actual position (green when inside the zone). Flick a switch and watch it work.
RXV2-0.9.400-rf-steps: Switches + Rescue-switch card: ranges now decode with Rotorflight's own encoding (signed 5 µs steps about 1500 - range 875-2125), fixing impossible values like ARM showing 3900 µs. Thanks to Malcolm's sharp eye.
RXV2-0.9.399-single-back: Fixed the twin 'Back to Rotorflight' buttons on the Rotorflight pages - each page keeps exactly one.
RXV2-0.9.398-modes: NEW: Switches page (Rotorflight menu) - what each transmitter switch makes the flight controller do (Rotorflight's Modes tab, in plain English). See, change, add and remove switch actions - Arm, Rescue, self-level, governor and more - each save verified. The Rescue page's switch card now links straight to the right row here.
RXV2-0.9.397-rescue-switch: Rescue screen now shows WHICH transmitter channel triggers rescue (read from the flight controller's Modes table), with the active range - and a loud warning if NO switch is assigned, because then rescue can never fire (Malcolm: 'it's critical').
RXV2-0.9.396-rescue-xref: Rescue screen: every label now also shows Rotorflight's own name for it in brackets (e.g. Levelling strength = Level gain), so you can cross-reference the configurator with no guesswork.
RXV2-0.9.395-rescue: NEW: Rescue screen (Rotorflight menu) - the safety net. Set per bank what happens when you flick the rescue switch: level & climb (or hold height), flip upright if inverted, the stage timings, collective bite and a hard collective ceiling - all in plain English, read from and written to the flight controller with every save verified. Included in phone backup & restore.
RXV2-0.9.394-sim-bind: You can now bind a receiver while it's in simulator mode: a 'Bind to a transmitter' button appears on the Simulator page. (A sim receiver's radio keeps listening, so it binds normally; the button was only ever on the home page before.)
RXV2-0.9.393-gear-ratio-label: Wording: the Setup button now reads 'failsafe, battery, gear ratio' (was 'gear').
RXV2-0.9.392-settings-moved: View channels is now just that - viewing channels. The gear ratio, battery voltage divider and failsafe settings have moved up to their own 'Receiver settings' page under Setup, where they belong.
RXV2-0.9.391-diag-sections: Tidier View-channels page: the live channel bars and the three unrelated settings (gear ratio, battery voltage divider, failsafe) are now grouped under clear 'Live channels' and 'Settings' section headings, each setting with its own subheading.
RXV2-0.9.390-tx-vbat-slow: The battery number on the V1 transmitter's screen now gets its own extra-slow (~7 s) averaging so it sits dead-still up there, while the phone app and the flight-log voltage trace keep the quicker, more responsive reading. Best of both.
RXV2-0.9.389-vbat-smooth: Steadier battery-voltage reading: the divider ADC now oversamples 32x per update (was 4x) plus a gentle 2-second smoothing, so the number sits rock-still even without the divider's filter capacitor - while still following real changes quickly enough for the flight voltage trace.
RXV2-0.9.388-tx-guard: Back up and Restore now refuse to run while the transmitter is ON, with a clear explanation - a backup taken under a live TX silently skipped the bank walk and saved less than everything (Malcolm's catch).
RXV2-0.9.387-nav-dedup: Tidier navigation (Malcolm's suggestion): the bottom 'Back to front screen' button is gone - the top-left Home button already does that job. Sub-pages keep their one-level-up Back button (e.g. WiFi back to Setup), which Home can't do.
RXV2-0.9.386-tail-label: Servos screen: servo 4 is now labelled TAIL servo (Rotorflight's fixed allocation: servos 1-3 swashplate, 4 tail).
RXV2-0.9.385-servos: NEW: Servos screen (Rotorflight menu) - each servo's centre (subtrim), travel limits, throw scale, direction, swash geometry correction, update rate and slow-motion time, read from and written to the flight controller with every save verified byte-for-byte. The crash-repair screen: swap a servo at the field, re-centre, set throws, fly.
RXV2-0.9.384-msp-wait: MSP wait window 400ms to 1200ms - chunked responses span several telemetry frames.
RXV2-0.9.383-msp-chunks: Groundwork for the Servos screen (and everything after): the receiver now reassembles chunked MSP responses from the flight controller, so replies bigger than one radio frame (like the full servo configuration) arrive intact instead of being silently dropped.
RXV2-0.9.382-fc-hint: Home page now hints when a flight controller is obeying but silent: 'check TELEMETRY is enabled in Rotorflight' - a fresh FC with telemetry off cannot be detected (it obeys channels but never speaks), which cost Malcolm a hunt on two new builds.
RXV2-0.9.381-no-pause: Spool-up now starts the INSTANT the motor comes back (Malcolm's report: 'a pause before it starts to move'). The USB joystick only shows the middle slice of the channel; the ramp was wasting seconds in the invisible saturated zones. It now jumps those instantly and spends the whole configured time in the visible sweep the simulator follows.
RXV2-0.9.380-two-speed: Two-speed spool-up (Malcolm's field report): a brief motor cut - bailing out of an autorotation mid-air - recovers on a fast governor rate (quarter of the ground time); a long cut (landed, sitting in the hold) restarts on the full slow ground spool. Chosen automatically from how long the power was off.
RXV2-0.9.379-json-fix: Fixes truncated spool-up status JSON (buffer was one size too small once the live diagnosis window was added) - the card could fail to load its settings on 0.9.377/378.
RXV2-0.9.378-torque-curve: Spool-up tail stab now follows real physics (Malcolm's observation): largest at the moment power returns - main-blade mass accelerating against a still-slow tail rotor - then dying away tangentially as the head reaches stable speed and tail authority builds.
RXV2-0.9.377-spool-debug: Spool-up tuned for LDRC's true 500-2500 channel range (times and tail clamp were sized for 1000-2000) plus a live diagnosis window in the API.
RXV2-0.9.376-motor-inv: Spool-up realism: added the 'High = motor OFF' switch for inverted motor channels (like Malcolm's ch6, where maximum means motor off). The governor ramp now works in power terms whichever way round your channel runs.
RXV2-0.9.375-motor-ch: HOTFIX for spool-up realism: it was slowing the throttle STICK channel, which on a helicopter is the COLLECTIVE - enabling it froze collective control. The spool now acts only on a dedicated Motor/governor channel you choose on the card (0 = off until set). Tip: open View channels and flip in/out of your autorotation bank - the bar that jumps is your motor channel.
RXV2-0.9.374-spool-next: Realistic spool-up moved to its proper home: the neXt controls & views page (RealFlight simulates its own governor, so the card only shows for neXt). Same feature as 0.9.373.
RXV2-0.9.373-spool-up: NEW for simulator pilots: Realistic spool-up (on the Sim controls page). When the motor comes back after an autorotation (or any throttle-hold), the head speed builds gradually like a real governor - adjustable 1-60 seconds - with an adjustable stab of tail while it accelerates, instead of the sim snapping instantly to full speed. Cutting the throttle stays instant, so entering autos is unchanged. Off by default; live-adjustable, no reboot.
RXV2-0.9.372-sim-failsafe: Simulator mode now obeys your saved failsafe positions: when the transmitter goes quiet, the sim's controls move to the posture you saved (Save failsafe on the View-channels page) instead of freezing at the last stick positions. Saving always worked - the sim just never applied it.
RXV2-0.9.264-fly-guard: Fly now is unavailable until a transmitter is actually connected - the button dims and explains itself, and lights up the moment your TX comes on. No more accidentally switching the radios off with nothing to fly. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.263-bind-escape: Bind mode gets an escape hatch: entering bind now puts the current pairing safely aside, and while bind mode is active the Bind button becomes 'Cancel bind - restore previous pairing' - a mistaken tap is fully undoable. Fly now is also truly one-tap-one-confirm: no more separate screen; the menu stays put, a green banner confirms, and the Fly button itself becomes the way back. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.262-quick-actions: FLY NOW and BIND are now one tap + one instant confirmation ('Disable WiFi & Bluetooth?' / 'Enter bind mode?') - the dialogs open immediately instead of pausing while data loads, and Bind no longer detours through a second page. Also: the aileron wave can no longer fire while you are turning the radios OFF, and pressing Fly now with no transmitter keeps the radios off instead of quietly reviving them 10 seconds later. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.261-keep-flights: Saved flights now SURVIVE updates: the three flight recordings are held in memory while the web pages are reflashed and written back afterwards, exactly as Rotorflight backups always were. Updating at the field no longer costs you your flight history. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.260-gap-position: The longest gap now says WHEN it struck ('55.1 ms at 00:00:12') so you can tell a connect-ritual tail from a mid-flight dropout at a glance. Also: the transmitter switch-off pause is now scrubbed permanently (turning the TX back on quickly can no longer resurrect it into the stats). Includes the 3-second handshake grace from 0.9.259. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.259-grace-3s: Link statistics now start when the connection is 3 seconds old (was 2 - a 55 ms handshake straggler remained), and the radio-swap count and per-radio times are re-baselined at the same moment, so the transmitter's connect ritual no longer inflates any flight figure. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.258-handshake-grace: THE 1-SECOND GAP, SOLVED FOR REAL: it was the V1 transmitter's own connect ritual - bind confirm and model-ID handshake pause its radio for about a second before the green light. The V1 transmitter has always hidden this by wiping its stats just after the green light; the receiver now applies the same wisdom - gap statistics only start once the connection is 2 seconds old. Also: a flight's R1/R2 radio times now stop at the last packet (no more growing on the bench). Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.257-ble-preheat: KILLS the mystery 1-second gap (finally - the black box breadcrumbs caught it): the Bluetooth radio's very first transmission does a one-off calibration that deafens the receiver chips for about a second. It used to fire mid-session when the transmitter was on from power-up; Bluetooth now starts at boot, before any link exists, so the deaf moment happens before the first packet. Also: a flight's per-radio times now stop counting at the last packet, so R1+R2 matches the flight duration. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.256-gap-hunt: Hunts the mystery 1-second link gap seen when the transmitter is on from power-up: a flash write fired at exactly t=5s used to freeze the processor mid-session - it now waits for a link-quiet moment. Also, any large gap on a live link is recorded in the event log with a timestamp, so the black box itself explains any future gap. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.255-save-label: The save button on the Output protocol page now tells the truth: it says 'Save' normally and only grows into 'Save & reboot' when you have actually selected a different protocol. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.254-armed-no-wave: Safety: the Bluetooth-ready wave is suppressed while the model is ARMED with a live transmitter link, so an in-flight brownout reboot can never wiggle the controls mid-air. Bench reboots with the transmitter on (disarmed) still wave. Includes 0.9.253's civilised save flow: instant-apply saves stay on the page; the reboot-wait screen only appears for a real protocol change. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.253-save-flow: Saving settings is now civilised: a save that applies instantly (wave channels, throttle/arming channel, CRSF rate, FC-telemetry) says 'Saved - applied instantly' and stays on the page; the reboot-wait screen only appears for a genuine protocol change, and over Bluetooth it waits for the app's automatic reconnection. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.252-wave-visible: Second-aileron wave now VISIBLE: a channel parked outside servo range (AUX channels rest at 500us before the TX is heard) waves around CENTRE instead of hugging its end-stop, where the movement was real in the data but invisible on the surface. Adds a Test-wave button next to the wave-channels setting, and saving settings from the phone app no longer risks a dead black page. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.251-wave-api: Adds POST /api/wave: fire the Bluetooth-ready wave on demand (refused while the transmitter link is live). Bench-test hook and 'which model is this?' finder. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.250-wave-polish: Wave fix: channels that sit at a low value (e.g. a second aileron on ch6, which boots at 500us) now get the FULL wave - previously the wiggle was clipped flat at the servo floor, so only channel 1 appeared to move. Every waved channel also returns EXACTLY to where it started when the wave ends (they were being left at the last wave position). The arming channel is never waved. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.249-wave-channels: The Bluetooth-ready wave is now configurable and universal: choose WHICH channels wave on the Output protocol page (e.g. 1,6 for a plane with two aileron servos; the throttle channel never waves), and the wave now fires EVERY time Bluetooth becomes available - power-on included - not just after switching the transmitter off. Also works on models with no captured failsafe. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.248-wave-fix: The aileron wave after switching off the transmitter now works on models with NO captured failsafe posture (it rides on the held servo positions instead) - previously it silently did nothing on such models. Includes everything from 0.9.247: update announcements and web-page delivery over Bluetooth at the field. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.247-field-updates: Field updates completed: with the phone app (iPhone 1.35 / Android 1.35), the home page now ANNOUNCES new firmware over Bluetooth at the field (the app fetches the release list with the phone's own internet) and one tap installs it - firmware AND web pages - over Bluetooth. Web pages now always ship with firmware even when installing from an older receiver page. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.223-fly-fix: Fixes the 'Re-enable WiFi & Bluetooth' button showing the fly-confirmation card instead of actually re-enabling (a later line of code was overwriting its action). Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.222-fly-menu: Radios-off mode gets a proper front door: from the RF-only screen you can now return to the menu WITHOUT re-enabling the radios, and while they're off the Fly-now slot becomes a big green 'Re-enable WiFi & Bluetooth' button. The Bluetooth badge hides while the radios are off (the receiver is only whispering down one kept link). Also fixes the kept Bluetooth link going mute after fly-arm — the return buttons now genuinely work. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.221-fly-ui: Fly-screen polish: the 'turns off WiFi & Bluetooth' note sits neatly under 'Fly now' instead of squashed beside it, and the return button on the RF-only screen now says 'Turn WiFi & Bluetooth back ON' in big friendly letters - it's rather important, after all. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.220-fly-ble: Fly now enters the Bluetooth era: the button says what it does (turns off WiFi AND Bluetooth), every screen names both radios, and when you're connected by Bluetooth the 'RF-only' screen keeps ONE quiet link alive (no advertising) so it can offer a Return-to-menu button - tap it and the receiver reboots with both radios back, the app reconnecting by itself. Close the app instead and that last link goes silent for interference-free flying. Also: firmware installs over Bluetooth now confirm before rebooting. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.219-update-test: No functional change - identical to 0.9.218 apart from the version number. Released to prove the new persistent update-offer works end to end (connect over Bluetooth, see the offer appear, tap to install).
RXV2-0.9.218-update-check: The 'Update available' offer no longer gets missed when you connect quickly after powering the receiver. The home page used to check for new firmware exactly once - if the receiver's WiFi was still coming up at that moment (typical in the first seconds after power-on) the check answered 'offline' and the offer silently never appeared, though a later connection (or another phone) would see it. The page now keeps quietly re-checking for a couple of minutes until the receiver is online, so the offer pops up as soon as it can be known. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.
RXV2-0.9.217-ble-name: ANDROID! The receiver now works with the new RXV2 Android app as well as the iPhone app. Bluetooth is far more dependable on every phone: replies are sent in chunks every device can swallow (some Androids quietly drop oversized packets even after promising a big one), sized to the connection's true negotiated limit, with a larger buffer pool so a whole page queues at once. Also fixes the Bluetooth scan NAME - the receiver now correctly advertises your model's name (e.g. 'BenchTest') instead of appearing nameless or as a stale cached name; a subtle ordering bug meant the name never fitted into the advertisement. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.
RXV2-0.9.212-ble-config: BLUETOOTH! Configure the receiver from the new RXV2 iPhone app over Bluetooth LE - no hotspot-joining dance, faster and more dependable than WiFi, and perfect at the field (the WiFi web setup is unchanged for everyone else). The View-channels page is now silky: the receiver PUSHES channel data continuously over Bluetooth, bars and the 3D helicopter animate smoothly through radio hiccups, and the ARMED indicator is live. Home page shows one pill per transceiver slot - green 'receiving' follows whichever radio carries your transmitter right now. Also: WiFi+Bluetooth coexistence boot-loop cured, wrapped-banner layout fixed, and every help screen explains the ways to connect. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.
RXV2-0.9.191-flight-save: Flights now SURVIVE A REBOOT. When a flight ends (link gone ~15s) the receiver writes it to flash (LittleFS) and keeps the last 3, so you can compare today with earlier flights. The Black box page gains a flight selector (Current / Previous / N flights ago, with each duration) that drives both the link stats and the graph. New endpoints: /api/flights.json (list) and /api/flightlog.json?f=N.
RXV2-0.9.190-graph-traces: Flight graph now plots four traces, each in its own colour with a labelled key showing the latest value and min-max: ESC temperature (red), head speed (blue), battery voltage (green) and current/amps (orange). Each line is auto-scaled to its own range so the shapes line up - you can see the battery sag and current spike as head speed and ESC temp rise. Current added to the receiver telemetry log.
RXV2-0.9.189-flight-graph: Phase 2 of post-flight analysis: the Black box page now plots a FLIGHT GRAPH - ESC temperature (left axis, red) and head speed (right axis, blue) over time, one sample/second, held from the last flight. Watch the ESC temp track head speed to catch a cooling/load problem before it bites. Receiver logs ~20 min in a ring buffer; served at /api/flightlog.json. No transmitter needed.
RXV2-0.9.188-link-stats: Phase 1 of post-flight analysis on the receiver: the Black box page now shows LINK statistics for the last flight - connection duration, average frame rate, packet count, average gap and LONGEST gap (colour-coded), plus a gap-distribution histogram. Computed on the receiver from the RF packet timing, so no transmitter needed after landing. Resets when a new flight begins. (Telemetry-vs-time graph is Phase 2.)
RXV2-0.9.187-fc-id-inflight: Fixes governor options missing after a flight. The receiver used to skip all FC probing while a TX link was live, so booting with the transmitter on for a flight meant it never learned the flight-controller API version - and the governor pages need API 12.9+ (RF 2.3). It now learns the FC identity ONCE even in flight (a few tiny non-blocking requests, no Configurator in the air), then stays quiet; the API value persists, so governor is available after landing. General Rotorflight options may still take a few seconds to appear after landing while WiFi re-enables and telemetry resumes - switching the TX on makes them appear at once.
RXV2-0.9.186-batt-icon: Adds the classic battery icon to the Black box status: it fills to the state-of-charge and colours green (>=50%), amber (>=20%) or red (low), matching the per-cell voltage reading. Purely visual, at-a-glance battery check.
RXV2-0.9.185-voltage-soc: Battery % is now a resting-voltage state-of-charge from the per-cell voltage, instead of the flight-controllers mAh-based figure (which reads ~full on the bench because little current has been drawn - e.g. 98% at 3.75 V/cell). Standard resting-LiPo curve: 3.75 V ~25%, 3.80 V ~40%, 4.20 V 100%. Note that it reads low under load.
RXV2-0.9.184-per-cell: Battery status now shows PER-CELL voltage (large), with the cell count auto-detected from the pack voltage (ceil(V/4.3) - reliable for storage or charged packs of any size). Also shows cell count (e.g. 4S), pack voltage and %. Colour cue: green at/above storage, amber getting low, red very low. Reminder to store at 3.80 V/cell.
RXV2-0.9.183-blackbox-status: Adds a live Status panel to the Black box page: battery VOLTAGE (large), pack %, current, mAh used, head speed, ESC temp and flight mode - all from the flight-controller telemetry, updating every 2s. Handy for a quick battery check with the model powered (the transmitter does not need to be on; just have WiFi up).
RXV2-0.9.182-restore-rates: Makes the transmitter backup/restore of Rates+Advanced behave like V1. When the TX restores both together it sends the basic batch AND the advanced batch; the receiver now writes BOTH (so the basic rates are actually restored), while an advanced-only EDIT still preserves the basic rates (no zeroing). Matches V1 exactly: basic is written on the combined save only when the TX actually sent it. PIDs, advanced PID and governor-profile restore were already full writes.
RXV2-0.9.181-sticky-block: Further reduces occasional all-zeros when reading params from the transmitter (seen most on governor profile). The receiver now keeps streaming the last-read block's cached values to the TX even after the read window ends - so lingering on a screen past the window, or a dropped request, shows the last good values (stale at worst) instead of zeros. FC re-polling still stops when the window closes, so no extra MSP load.
RXV2-0.9.180-fc-keepalive: Fixes the web UI losing its Rotorflight options after the transmitter is used then switched off (until a reboot). On CRSF, signal loss detaches the output UART (so the FC sees the dropout) - but that also kills the FC RX line, so MSP stops and the flight-controller detection times out. The receiver now keeps the UART attached whenever WiFi is up (bench/config mode, where there is no transmitter by design and you need MSP). In-flight failsafe is unchanged - WiFi is off in flight.
RXV2-0.9.179-gov-global: Fixes the governor GLOBAL (config) screen showing nothing on the transmitter. The receiver was discarding the whole MSP_GOVERNOR_CONFIG response unless it was at least 42 bytes, but RF 2.3 can report a different length - and only bytes up to 32 are actually read (the bypass curve at 33+ is just preserved on write). Now accepts any response reaching byte 32, so the global settings populate.
RXV2-0.9.178-tx-governor: Adds GOVERNOR editing from the transmitter (profile + config), RF 2.3+ only. Profile via MSP_GOVERNOR_PROFILE/SET (148/149); config via MSP_GOVERNOR_CONFIG/SET (142/143) followed by an FC reboot so it takes effect (like V1). Completes full Rotorflight parity from the handset: rates, advanced rates, PIDs, advanced PIDs, governor - all readable and writable from the TX as well as the iPhone.
RXV2-0.9.177-adv-pid: Adds ADVANCED PID editing from the transmitter (read + write): the full Dynamics/bandwidth/cutoff/limit set (26 values) via MSP_PID_PROFILE / MSP_SET_PID_PROFILE, mapped through the scattered profile offsets. Read-modify-write preserves untouched fields. That is rates, advanced rates, PIDs and advanced PIDs all editable from the handset - governor next.
RXV2-0.9.176-timing: Reduces the occasional all-zeros when reading params from the transmitter. Removed the post-write cache blanking (the re-poll refreshes the saved values anyway), tightened the FC re-poll to ~50ms (was 80ms, matching V1), and shortened the stuck-fetch retry from 400ms to 250ms. Any remaining rare zeros are a dropped request packet from the TX (re-trigger to fix).
RXV2-0.9.175-adv-preserve: Fix: saving ADVANCED rates from the transmitter no longer zeroes that bank's BASIC rates (and vice-versa). Each rates screen now writes only its own fields via read-modify-write; the other fields are preserved from the FC. Previously the advanced save also wrote the basic-rate fields from staged values that could be zero (e.g. a lost batch packet), clobbering the bank.
RXV2-0.9.174-tx-pids: Adds PID editing from the transmitter (read + write). 17 PID values (P/I/D/FF per axis, boosts, HSI offsets) read via MSP_PID and written via MSP_SET_PID, using the same continuous-re-poll engine as rates. Governor next.
RXV2-0.9.173-adv-fix: Fixes the advanced-rates setpoint boost gain/cutoff scramble on the transmitter. The MSP RC_TUNING boost tail is interleaved per axis (Roll gain, Roll cutoff, Pitch gain, Pitch cutoff ...), not grouped - corrected both the read (TX now shows the Configurator values) and the write-back.
RXV2-0.9.172-adv-rates: Adds ADVANCED RATES editing from the transmitter (response time, setpoint-boost gain/cutoff, yaw dynamics), and fixes the intermittent all-zeros on bank switch. Like V1, the receiver now RE-POLLS the flight-controller continuously (~80ms) while the transmitter is reading a rates block, so a bank change or a single missed MSP round-trip no longer leaves the TX reading zeros. Rates + advanced are written together (combined MSP_SET_RC_TUNING) preserving untouched fields.
RXV2-0.9.171-rfver: Fixes the rate FACTORS shown on the transmitter. Ack slot 31 now reports the real Rotorflight version (1 = RF2.2, 2 = RF2.3) instead of a flat 1, so the TX picks the correct 2.3 factor table - rates now read exactly as the Configurator (Roll 160/20/20, Yaw 400/20/20, Collective 6.0/48/0) instead of the 2.2-scaled 320/200/0.20. Also relabels the TX columns to Rate/Shape/Expo on 2.3.
RXV2-0.9.170-tx-rates: NEW: edit Rotorflight RATES from the transmitter (not just the iPhone). A V1-compatible transmitter can now read and set the rate values over the radio link - the receiver fetches/writes them to the flight-controller over MSP. Built on a new non-blocking parameter engine (TxParams.h) ported byte-exact from V1, so it never stalls the RC link. RATES first; PIDs and governor to follow. iPhone editing unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.169-nocache-js: Fixed stale-UI-after-update: app.js and style.css were cached by the browser for a whole day (max-age=86400), so a freshly-updated page could call helpers the old cached app.js did not have yet (e.g. the new Save-confirmation box silently did nothing). They now revalidate every load like the HTML pages do. NOTE: after THIS update do one hard-refresh (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R) to clear the previously-cached app.js; subsequent UI updates take effect immediately.
RXV2-0.9.168-gear-msg: Save gear ratio now pops a confirmation box ("Gear ratio = <n> saved!") instead of only a quiet status line. Added a shared single-button LDRC.alert() helper for tidy acknowledgements.
RXV2-0.9.167-fs-crsf: Failsafe now defers to the flight-controller on CRSF. A Rotorflight FC overrules receiver-streamed channels on signal loss (its own failsafe is the authority over CRSF), so on CRSF the receiver no longer streams the saved failsafe - it lets the FC take over (configure it in Rotorflight's Failsafe tab). The saved failsafe is KEPT and still applied on signal loss for SBUS / FBUS / IBUS / PPM models that rely on it. No-transmitter boot is still always disarmed-safe.
RXV2-0.9.166-fs-apply: Completes the failsafe: the saved positions are now applied on IN-FLIGHT signal loss. If the transmitter link is lost after having been connected, the receiver drives every channel to your saved failsafe set and keeps streaming them as valid RC, so the flight-controller holds your chosen failsafe (set the model to a safe posture - motor off for a heli - before saving). If no failsafe is saved, behaviour is unchanged (the FC runs its own failsafe). A no-transmitter power-up still always uses the guaranteed disarmed-safe default, never these values.
RXV2-0.9.165-headspeed: Two telemetry items added like V1: HEAD SPEED and ESC TEMPERATURE, read from the CRSF telemetry the flight-controller streams (enable RPM + Temperature sensors in Rotorflight telemetry). Head speed = motor RPM / gear ratio, with a configurable GEAR RATIO on the View-channels page (1.0 = direct drive). SAFETY FIX: the receiver now NEVER boots to your saved failsafe positions (those can have the arm/safety switch off); a no-transmitter power-up always uses the guaranteed disarmed-safe default (sticks centred, AUX low). The failsafe Save still stores your positions for later use.
RXV2-0.9.164-failsafe: Adds a configurable failsafe (no-transmitter) posture, like V1. On the View-channels page there is now a Failsafe section: set every stick and switch where you want the model to sit with no transmitter (e.g. disarmed, motor off) and tap Save - those exact positions are stored in NVS and output when the receiver is powered up without a transmitter. Clear reverts to the built-in safe default (sticks centred, AUX low). Replaces guessing with your real safe positions - e.g. your AUX1 safety channel.
RXV2-0.9.163-safe-boot: Safer power-up with no transmitter. Until a transmitter connects, the receiver used to output every channel at mid (1500us) - which a flight-controller reads as a centred, ARMED link, so a heli FC tries to stabilise and the swashplate hunts up and down. It now boots into a disarmed/safe posture instead: sticks centred (ch1-5 = 1500) and all AUX channels low (ch6-16 = 500), so any arm/mode switch reads OFF and nothing spins. As soon as the transmitter connects, real values take over; signal loss after a link still holds the last good values. (Assumes the usual arm-switch-low = disarmed convention.)
RXV2-0.9.162-bind-live: The front screen now updates the bind status by itself. Before, after a successful bind the LED went steady (correct) but the home page still said 'Bind mode' until you left and re-opened it. The page now re-checks every few seconds, so it flips to 'Bound' (and clears the amber bind banner) within a couple of seconds of binding — no navigation needed. Same live-refresh that the Rotorflight button uses.
RXV2-0.9.161-deadband-x10: Fixes a factor-of-10 on the Rates page 'Dynamic deadband filter' (yaw dynamics). It is stored in deci-Hz, so a value of 60 means 6.0 Hz — the page was showing the raw 60 instead of 6.0. Now displayed and saved in Hz to match the Configurator. The other yaw-dynamics fields were already correct.
RXV2-0.9.160-actual-cols: Tidies the Rates page for the ACTUAL rate type (Rotorflight 2.2 default) to match the official Configurator: columns are now Centre / Max Rate / Expo / Max Vel (instead of the old generic Centre / Expo / Max plus two always-zero Resp/Accel columns). Values were already correct; this just lays them out the same as the Configurator, like the ROTORFLIGHT type already does.
RXV2-0.9.159-rf22-detect: Fixes Rotorflight 2.2 detection. The receiver was mis-mapping the FC API version, so a 2.2 flight-controller (API 12.8) was tagged as "1.x" and ALL Rotorflight options disappeared. The mapping is corrected (API 12.8 = RF 2.2, 12.9 = RF 2.3, etc.), so 2.2 is recognised and its config pages appear and read the right version. Following V1: on 2.2 you get everything EXCEPT the two Governor pages (governor needs Rotorflight 2.3 / API 12.9), which are now hidden on 2.2 rather than opening to a disabled page.
RXV2-0.9.158-rf-btn-live: The home-screen "Rotorflight config" button now appears (and disappears) on its own as the flight-controller is detected, instead of only being decided once when the page opened. Detecting an FC over CRSF can take a few seconds, so previously the button was intermittently missing and only showed up if you re-opened the front screen after it had been found. Now the page re-checks every few seconds. (Note: this only reveals the button once the receiver actually hears the FC — if it never appears, the receiver isn't getting any telemetry back from the FC, which is a wiring/return-path issue, not this.)
RXV2-0.9.157-rates-curve: Cosmetic follow-up to 0.9.156: the Rates preview curve now plots Roll/Pitch/Yaw on one shared deg/s scale (so Yaw at 400 visibly rises above Roll/Pitch at 250, like the official Configurator) while Collective keeps its own scale. Numbers were already correct; this just makes the curve picture match.
RXV2-0.9.156-rf23-rates: Fixes the Rates page for Rotorflight 2.3. RF 2.3 defaults to a new rates type (#6, 'ROTORFLIGHT') that didn't exist in 2.2; our page was still showing the old generic columns (Centre/Expo/Max…) and the wrong scaling, so both the headings AND the numbers were wrong. The page is now rate-type aware: for the ROTORFLIGHT type it shows the correct columns — Rate, Shape, Expo, Max Vel — matching the official Configurator exactly (e.g. Roll 250 / 12 / 40, Yaw 400 / 12 / 50, Collective 12.5 / 12 / 0). Saving back is scaled correctly and now also preserves the new 2.3 cyclic-ring/polar settings instead of dropping them. Other rate types keep the previous columns.
RXV2-0.9.155-factory-card: Readability fix: the 'Factory defaults' box on the WiFi page had a near-transparent background, so its text was hard to read over the background photo. It now uses the same pale card background as every other section (keeping its red border and warning styling so it still reads as a danger zone).
RXV2-0.9.154-wifi-1s: Tunes the auto-WiFi from 0.9.153 and documents it. The boot listen-for-transmitter window is now 1 second (was 5): WiFi comes up almost instantly when there's no transmitter, which means the transmitter must be switched ON before the receiver to run radio-only — and switching the transmitter on first is normal RC practice anyway. Adds a clear 'WiFi and your transmitter' section to the WiFi page Help so users understand why WiFi may be off (a transmitter was on at switch-on) and how it returns by itself ~10s after the link is lost.
RXV2-0.9.153-wifi-auto: WiFi is now managed automatically around the transmitter. (1) At power-up the receiver listens for the transmitter for 5 seconds; if it hears one, it switches WiFi OFF for the session and runs radio-only — the cleanest band and full 501 Hz. (2) If, in that radio-only mode, the transmitter link is then lost for 10 seconds (you've landed, or switched the TX off), WiFi comes back on by itself so you can reach the receiver from your phone — no power-cycle needed. Simulator sessions keep WiFi on throughout (so you can still use the web UI while driving the sim). Note: a real in-air dropout lasting 10 s would also re-enable WiFi mid-flight; the threshold is easy to raise if you'd prefer a longer wait.
RXV2-0.9.152-ap-only-ux: Polishes the new 'AP mode only' option. (1) Plain-English explanation on the WiFi page — spells out that AP mode means the receiver makes its own little WiFi network your phone joins directly (no home router), why you'd tick it at the field, and that you'll need to switch your phone's WiFi after saving. (2) The save page no longer sits there waiting: when you turn AP-only on it stops polling the old address (which has gone) and instead clearly tells you to open your phone's WiFi settings, join the receiver's network (named), and go to 192.168.4.1. (3) Bug fix: the status page now shows the receiver's REAL access-point name (its model name, e.g. your renamed receiver) instead of always showing the old default 'LDRC_RX'.
RXV2-0.9.150-ap-only: Adds an 'AP mode only' tick-box to the WiFi page. When on, the receiver skips trying to join your home WiFi and comes straight up as its own access point — handy at the flying field, where the home network is miles away and the receiver would otherwise spend every boot fruitlessly retrying it. Your saved home SSID/password are kept; just untick it to use home WiFi again. The choice is saved in NVS and survives reboots/updates.
RXV2-0.9.149-wifi-advice: Adds a setup tip on the WiFi page (and its help): WiFi is steadiest with the transmitter switched off, because the control radio and WiFi share the 2.4GHz band and a live transmitter link can make WiFi drop in and out. Advises using the transmitter or the phone when you can — both together works fine, but expect WiFi to be less consistent. Text only; no behaviour change. (Includes the data/web files, so the page updates.)
RXV2-0.9.148-flash-fixed: FIXES the channels flashing to zero on the Configurator. Root cause, pinned down by on-board logging: whenever WiFi tried to reconnect — and WiFi drops a lot while flying because the radio desenses it — the reconnect ran inline and FROZE the main loop for ~208ms each attempt, long enough to pause RC output and starve the radio, so the flight-controller saw a brief RX-loss and the channels flashed to zero, then recovered. WiFi reconnection is now fully non-blocking: the loop never stalls and RC output stays continuous no matter how much WiFi flaps. Verified over 20+ minutes connected with WiFi flapping throughout — zero output stalls, zero spurious drops. (Also rolls up the supporting robustness work from 0.9.136-0.9.140: failsafe keyed off the real packet stream, a short board-ID burst then continuous telemetry like V1, gentler dual-radio failover, out-of-range frames rejected so the last good values are held, and no FC version-polling while a link is live.)
RXV2-0.9.140-no-fc-probe-flying: Found the real cause of the channels flashing to zero in the Rotorflight Configurator. The actual RC output was never glitching (steady 250Hz, link solid) — it was only the Configurator's *display*. The receiver was polling the flight-controller over MSP every few seconds to read its firmware version; that made the receiver a second MSP 'master' on the FC, colliding with the Configurator's own MSP polling of the same FC, so the Configurator periodically read an empty frame and showed all channels at zero. The receiver now never probes the FC while a transmitter link is live (it already behaved this way on shipping firmware; a dev-only setting was bypassing it). FC-version detection still happens when not flying, which is when the web page needs it. Note: the model itself was always controlled correctly throughout — this was a bench-display artifact, not a flight risk.
RXV2-0.9.139-hold-last-good: Channels flashing to zero, fixed the way V1 does it: hold the last good value. Two V1 behaviours the receiver was missing are now restored. (1) Crazy-value rejection: the transmitter periodically sends non-channel frames (bind/ID/parameter data); if one was misread as channel data it drove every channel to zero for an instant. Like V1's CheckForCrazyValues, any decoded frame with a channel outside the legal 500-2500us range is now rejected and the last good values are held. (2) The output no longer goes briefly silent on a momentary gap: the failsafe timeout is raised from 500ms to V1's 1500ms, and below it the receiver keeps streaming the held channel values (exactly as V1 keeps sending its SBUS frames) instead of detaching the CRSF line. True signal loss (>1.5s) still drops the link so the flight-controller can fail-safe.
RXV2-0.9.138-swap-storm-fix: The actual cause of the channels flashing to zero. When the active radio missed packets for a moment the receiver would try the other transceiver — correct — but it kept re-trying every 50ms in a tight storm (~20 swaps/second), and each swap briefly stops listening and reconfigures, which tore down the CRSF output stream long enough for the flight-controller to register a momentary RX-loss (the flash). It also flooded the event log so nothing else could be seen. Now: it tries each transceiver once per glitch, then — if no packet comes back (transmitter gone/out of range) — backs off to a slow once-a-second probe instead of storming, and re-arms instant failover the moment a real packet returns. Dead-link swaps no longer spam the log. Fast genuine failover between two good transceivers is unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.137-mac-burst-telemetry: The real fix for channels flashing to zero every ~10-15s with the sticks still (0.9.136 only moved the symptom). Root cause: the receiver was broadcasting its board ID to the transmitter continuously whenever you weren't actively moving a stick, and never sending telemetry — so the transmitter, starved of telemetry, hiccuped the link about every 10-15s (a brief RX-loss that flashed every channel to zero) and also never showed the RX version or the per-transceiver active-time counters until you wiggled a stick. Now the board ID is sent only as a short dense burst at the start of each connection (and re-sent on every reconnect), exactly like V1, then telemetry flows continuously. Result: rock-steady channels when not moving, and the version + counters appear immediately without touching the sticks. Note: the transmitter's 'Model IDs' identify screen now re-reads the ID on reconnect rather than continuously.
RXV2-0.9.136-failsafe-flash-fix: Fixes all channels briefly flashing to zero in the flight-controller (e.g. Rotorflight Configurator) every few seconds while the sticks are held still — a momentary false RXLOSS. The receiver was deciding 'link lost' from the last packet that carried channel data, but with the sticks still the transmitter sends only changed channels, so the gaps between changes (filled with parameter/no-change packets) made the link look dropped for an instant. Failsafe is now judged from the actual packet stream from the bound transmitter (which never stops while connected), so the channels stay rock-steady when you're not moving the sticks. Important for steady hovers.
RXV2-0.9.135-radio-timer-fix: Fixes the per-transceiver 'active time' counters on the TX screen sitting frozen at 0 on a solid link. The active radio's dwell time is now accrued continuously every loop (not via a live-delta that didn't land on a no-swap link), so one counter always ticks once per second while connected — matching V1.
RXV2-0.9.134-sim-wifi-top: Refines 0.9.133: instead of a separate button lower down, simulator mode now repurposes the existing top 'Fly now' button as 'Turn off WiFi — less interference' (same WiFi-off-until-reboot action, kept at the top where the Fly button lives). One control, one place, in both flying and sim use.
RXV2-0.9.133-sim-wifi-off: Simulator mode gains a 'Turn off WiFi' button (it only appears while in sim mode). Tapping it cuts WiFi to reduce radio interference while the simulator keeps running over USB — handy on a noisy bench, though not as critical as the Fly button before real flying. WiFi (and phone control) automatically comes back on the next power-cycle/reboot.
RXV2-0.9.132-update-bar: The firmware-update 'Installing…' screen now shows the same green progress bar as the simulator reboot screen (fills over ~30 s, snaps to full the moment the receiver is back) instead of a seconds counter, and its redundant Return-to-menu button is gone — it returns to the home screen by itself.
RXV2-0.9.131-reboot-bar: The 'Rebooting…' screen when starting/stopping simulator mode now shows a progress bar (fills over a few seconds, snaps to full the moment the receiver is back) instead of a seconds counter, and the now-redundant Return-to-menu button is gone — it returns to the home screen by itself.
RXV2-0.9.130-check-size: Fixes the update check failing ('network error') and the long pause entering simulator mode. The receiver was proxying the entire local + public manifests (~95 versions each, ~76 KB total) which choked it. Now the manifests are trimmed to the newest 12 versions, and the receiver skips any manifest that's still oversized — so the check stays small and fast. Rollback to recent versions is unaffected.
RXV2-0.9.129-no-back-btn: Removed the now-redundant 'Return to menu' button from the bottom of the pages — the floating 🏠 home button (top-left) does that from anywhere, no scrolling. Each page's Help (?) now reminds you the 🏠 button is the way back.
RXV2-0.9.128-btn-clearance: Every page now starts its content just below the floating Home/Help buttons, so the bigger buttons no longer overlap titles, cards or text at the top of any screen.
RXV2-0.9.127-bigger-btns: Made the floating Home (🏠) and Help (?) buttons bigger — easier to spot and tap.
RXV2-0.9.126-home-btn: Every page now has a fixed home button (🏠, top-left, mirroring the ? help button) that jumps straight back to the front menu — no more scrolling to the bottom to find Return to menu. Shown on all screens except the home page itself.
RXV2-0.9.125-check-retry: Makes the firmware check robust to a transient blip: it now retries once (after the receiver has had a moment to settle its WiFi, e.g. just after a reboot) before giving up. Fixes the spurious 'Network error talking to the receiver' on the firmware page and makes the 'Update now?' dialog appear reliably.
RXV2-0.9.124-update-prompt: When you open a receiver, it now checks for newer firmware straight away and, if there is some, pops an 'Update now?' dialog (installed vs available shown) instead of just a banner. Tap Update now and it downloads, flashes and reboots itself, then returns to the home screen — one tap, no firmware page needed. The banner remains as a tap-to-update fallback; Later dismisses it. (The check still defers while a transmitter link is live, so it never interrupts flying.)
RXV2-0.9.123-fly-bind-guards: Two home-screen fixes. 'Fly now' now disables WiFi directly — one tap, with a friendly confirm that also shows your live link status (it used to just open a page where you had to find a second button). 'Start Bind mode' is now guarded: if the receiver is already bound/connected it warns before erasing the bind and dropping the link (so you can't do it by accident); unbound, it still binds straight away.
RXV2-0.9.122-status-led: Adds support for an external status LED on the D4 pad: OFF = bound but no link, ON = connected & receiving, 2 Hz flash = binding. Only active when transceiver 3 is absent (D4 is radio 3's CE on triple-radio boards, so those are unaffected — auto-detected). LED is assumed wired pad->resistor->LED->GND (active-high); tell me if yours is inverted.
RXV2-0.9.121-help-per-sim: The ? help on the controls & views screen now matches the simulator you opened: neXt gets its own help (its keys, why there are no Select/Up/Down buttons, and the Mac Input-Monitoring steps), RealFlight keeps its full controls-and-views help.
RXV2-0.9.120-simple-look: Cleaner look everywhere: all the tiny technical small print (ch 12 - 833us, F3, Keypad +, ...) is gone from the controls and the key buttons — just clear labels now. RealFlight's key buttons are the same bigger size as neXt's. (The key assigned to each button is still shown in the editor.)
RXV2-0.9.119-next-clean: neXt's screen no longer shows the Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset buttons — they're RealFlight User-Interface bindings and do nothing in neXt. The neXt key buttons are bigger to use the space (and the page skips the now-pointless button polling, kinder to the radio). RealFlight's screen is unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.118-nice-confirm: The are-you-sure box for starting/leaving simulator mode is now a friendly colourful card in the app's own style (with a big green Yes and a Cancel), replacing the browser's grey utilitarian confirm dialog. Tap outside it to dismiss.
RXV2-0.9.117-prof-front: The simulator choice now lives ONLY on the home screen: the RealFlight / neXt switch has been removed from the controls & views screen, whose title now simply shows which simulator is active (e.g. 'neXt — controls & views'). Tapping a home button always opens with the right key set; to change simulator, return to the menu.
RXV2-0.9.116-reboot-ux: No more white screen when toggling simulator mode: the phone now shows 'Rebooting — please wait...' immediately (drawn before the toggle is even sent, so it cannot blank), counts the seconds, then returns to the home screen by itself — with a Return-to-menu button there throughout. And the home menu now has TWO simulator buttons — RealFlight and neXt — each opening the controls & views screen with that simulator's key set selected.
RXV2-0.9.115-return-fix: Sim-mode toggle (and every other reboot page) now reliably returns to the home screen: a Return-to-menu button is always shown (one tap recovers it — never close-and-reload again), polling starts sooner and waits longer, the redirect dodges stale caches, and coming back to a backgrounded tab re-checks immediately. Also the Simulator switch (RealFlight / neXt) above the camera buttons is now big and obvious with a 'Simulator:' label — it was too subtle to spot before.
RXV2-0.9.114-next-keys: The neXt profile now comes pre-filled with neXt 2.087's real keys (from its Settings -> Misc list): New model, Engine, Pause, Self level, Trainer, Piro trainer, Time scale, Set spawn, Prev model/scenery, Landing gear, flight Conditions 1-4, Mute, Music, Recorder, Screenshot, Chat, Menu. All editable per profile as before; anything you'd already saved for neXt is kept.
RXV2-0.9.113-sim-profiles: Two simulators, two key sets: new RealFlight / neXt chips above the camera buttons switch between separate view-key profiles, each remembered on the phone. RealFlight keeps its pre-filled keys (and your edits); neXt starts empty — select it and tap Edit view keys to add keys from neXt's keyboard list. Chosen deliberately over USB host auto-detection, which is unreliable (and wrong under a VM).
RXV2-0.9.112-mac-help: Help now covers using the simulator on a Mac (neXt etc.): quit the Keyboard Setup Assistant, and crucially enable your simulator in System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Input Monitoring (then restart it) — macOS hides the sticks from the sim until you do, because the device is part keyboard. Help-text only; no behaviour change.
RXV2-0.9.111-view-colours: Every camera/view button now has its own colour, so you can find a favourite by colour at a glance. Colours are fixed to each button slot (your favourite stays the same colour), and the editor shows each slot's colour dot.
RXV2-0.9.110-equal-pills: Select and Cancel are now each full-width — the same size as Reset; Up/Down triangles a touch smaller to make room.
RXV2-0.9.109-ctl-fill: Controls screen: all the buttons grow a little more to use the spare white space — wider/taller Up & Down triangles, taller Select/Cancel/Reset with larger text. Scroll behaviour unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.108-touch-fix: Scrolling fixed: a vertical swipe now scrolls the page even when it starts on the big Up/Down triangles (scrolling never fires them; a quick tap still does). Up/Down triangles made a bit smaller, Select/Cancel/Reset a bit bigger.
RXV2-0.9.107-big-ctl: Controls now FILL the first screen (huge Up/Down triangles + bigger Select/Cancel/Reset, with Reset full-width) so you can hit them without looking at the phone; scroll down for the views. Views expanded with RealFlight's other commands: Look at ground, Zoom reset, Follow/Pivot/Orbit cam, Next pit view, Zoom/Move mode, Kill engine, Flight failures, Screenshot, Record, Mute — all editable, and your earlier key edits are kept. Also fixes the Up/Down labels overlapping.
RXV2-0.9.106-ctl-size: Tuned the RealFlight controls & views screen: bigger controls — especially the Up/Down triangles — so you can hit Up/Down repeatedly while watching the sim on a TV across the room, with the camera/view buttons made a little smaller to balance. Cosmetic only.
RXV2-0.9.105-rf-ui: RealFlight controls and Views are now ONE home-menu item opening a single screen: controls up top (Select/Cancel/Reset as smaller ovals, Up/Down as up/down triangles you press & hold to repeat), the camera/view buttons below, then a darker 'Edit view keys' button. Cosmetic only — same buttons, channels, keys and behaviour.
RXV2-0.9.104-edit-btn: Views page: moved the Edit button down below the camera buttons so it no longer sits under the top-right ? Help button. Nothing else changed — same buttons, keys and mappings.
RXV2-0.9.103-rf-views: Views page defaults are now RealFlight 9.5's real View Commands (read from its Keyboard Commands dialog): Chase/Fixed/Nose cam = F3/F1/F2, Cockpit = F4, Cycle cam = C, Zoom in/out = keypad +/-, Windsock = Up arrow. Tap 'Reset to defaults' to load them; the editor still lets you map any key/combo to any RealFlight command.
RXV2-0.9.102-views-editor: The Views page now has an on-screen Edit button: set each button's label and pick its key from a friendly dropdown (Ctrl/Shift/Alt too), Save — stored on the phone, no re-flashing. So you can map the buttons to RealFlight's real view shortcuts yourself.
RXV2-0.9.101-keyboard: Sim mode is now a USB composite device: the existing gamepad PLUS a standard keyboard. New 'Views (camera)' phone page sends keyboard shortcuts (next view, zoom, cockpit/chase, etc.) to RealFlight — keycodes editable in the page. Gamepad report unchanged (a one-time RealFlight re-detect of the composite device aside). Keystrokes are non-blocking and don't affect the channel rate.
RXV2-0.9.100-reset-ch10: Swapped Reset and Select channels: Reset now on channel 10 (a switchable channel on the transmitter), Select on channel 14. Reset is the one you most want on a physical switch. Channels now: 10=Reset, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Select; ch9 still free for autorotation.
RXV2-0.9.99-tap-reliable: Makes the RealFlight-controls phone buttons more reliable: a tap now fires 3 times over ~180 ms (so an occasional dropped WiFi request no longer loses the press), and the button pulse is longer (250 ms) so the sim can't miss the edge. The firmware merges the repeats into one clean press — never a multi-fire.
RXV2-0.9.98-reset-ch14: Moved the RealFlight-controls Reset button from channel 9 to channel 14 (joystick button 6), leaving channel 9 free for RealFlight's helicopter autorotation. Channels now: 10=Select, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Reset. Page-only change; no re-calibration. You'll need to put the Reset switch on TX ch14 and re-bind Reset in RealFlight.
RXV2-0.9.97-usb-revert: Reverts the 0.9.96 non-blocking USB write — it halved the TX frame rate while flying the sim (≈200 vs 500 with sim off). The blocking write yields the CPU and paces the loop, which the radio link needs. Back to the proven behaviour. Keeps the 'RealFlight controls' rename and the return-to-home fix.
RXV2-0.9.96-ui-polish: Front-menu 'Sim controls' renamed to 'RealFlight controls' (those buttons are RealFlight's UI functions). After toggling simulator mode, the reboot page now waits for the receiver to be solidly back before returning to the home screen, instead of landing on a blank page. Also makes the USB sim write non-blocking so it can't stall the loop.
RXV2-0.9.95-loop-diag: Diagnostic build: adds loop_hz (main-loop iterations/sec) and loop_max_us (worst loop stall) to /api/state.json, to tell a CPU/servicing limit from an RF problem when chasing dropped frames. No functional change.
RXV2-0.9.94-wifi-quiet: Sim mode now runs WiFi at much lower power (8.5 dBm vs 19.5) so it stops desensitising the nRF24 receiver sitting right beside it — the cause of the short range and dropped frames when driving the sim (WiFi and the TX link share 2.4 GHz). Should markedly lift the frame rate and range. Normal mode keeps full WiFi reach. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.93-bind-restore: Reverts the 0.9.92 loop change (servicing the radio 3x per loop), which disturbed the timing-sensitive bind/hop handshake and stopped the transmitter binding. Back to the proven 0.9.91 radio servicing. Keeps the lighter Sim-controls polling. Proper fix (a dedicated radio core) to follow.
RXV2-0.9.92-link-fix: Fixes a reluctant / flaky TX link when a web page was open during sim use. The radio is now serviced before AND after the web server (and after the USB sim write), so a slow web request can no longer make the receiver miss an FHSS hop or ack. The Sim controls page also polls 3x more gently and pauses when hidden. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.91-menu-fit: Sim controls: the Return-to-menu button is now full-width but a normal height, so the five function buttons (Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset) grow taller to fill the screen. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.90-pad-menu: Sim controls tidy-up: all six buttons now exactly the same size, with a full-size 'Return to menu' button at the bottom (the tiny top link is gone). Up is pale blue and Down dark blue for quick contrast. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.89-big-pad: Sim controls is now one tall column of big, easy-to-hit targets filling the screen, in order Select · Up · Down · Cancel · Reset — Reset largest at the bottom, like the spacebar. Same colours and Up/Down auto-repeat. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.88-sim-pad: Sim controls redesigned as a proper pad: big red Reset, green Select, amber Cancel, and a stacked ▲/▼ Up/Down rocker. Up and Down now AUTO-REPEAT — hold the on-screen button (or a TX switch on ch12/ch13) to scroll a menu continuously. Joystick descriptor unchanged (8 buttons), so no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.87-ui-buttons: Sim controls page now shows exactly RealFlight's 5 User Interface functions — Reset, Select, Cancel, Up, Down (ch9→Reset … ch13→Down) — instead of generic labels. The joystick is unchanged (still 8 HID buttons under the hood), so no re-calibration is needed.
RXV2-0.9.86-sim-buttons: Sim mode gains 8 function buttons on the USB joystick — fire them from the new 'Sim controls' phone page OR from your transmitter's switches on channels 9-16 (ch9→button1 … ch16→button8). Bind each to a sim function (reset, pause, view…) in your sim's controller setup, and control the sim with no keyboard. Adding buttons changes the joystick, so it needs one re-calibration in the sim.
RXV2-0.9.85-fresh-ui: Web pages are now sent no-store, so a freshly-updated UI appears immediately instead of the browser (iOS Safari especially) showing a stale cached copy — no hard-refresh needed.
RXV2-0.9.84-fs-auto: The receiver now derives its web-filesystem URL from the firmware URL when the page doesn't supply it, so it pulls its own web files on the next update even from a stale page — updating twice fully self-heals an out-of-date UI, no computer needed. Backups still preserved.
RXV2-0.9.83-fs-ota: OTA install now also flashes the matching web/data filesystem (and preserves your Rotorflight backups), so the web UI travels with the firmware on every update — no separate uploadfs needed. First release that ships a littlefs.bin.
RXV2-0.9.82-tx-happy: Firmware-update check no longer stalls the radio while the TX link is live (it was starving radioPoll and dropping the transmitter); shorter idle timeouts.
RXV2-0.9.81-wifi-heal: WiFi self-heals from AP-only — retries the home network every 20 s when it has saved credentials, instead of staying stranded. Plus a big SIMULATOR-MODE-ON home banner.
RXV2-0.9.80-sim-safe: Drive-simulator-over-USB now disables the flight-controller output (D6 stays silent) so a real model can't be flown from sim mode; default channel map shown as a tidy 1:1.
RXV2-0.9.79-usb-sim-remap: Adds the Remap-channels page for simulator mode (feed any of the 8 sim outputs from any received channel, with live bars).
RXV2-0.9.78-usb-sim: First release with Drive-simulator-over-USB: the receiver can present as a USB HID joystick for a PC flight sim, driven by the channels it receives — no separate dongle.
RXV2-0.9.224-crsf-rate: Adds a CRSF frame-rate setting on the Output protocol page (250/100/50 Hz). Lower it to 100 Hz for CRSF-to-PWM servo converters whose firmware misbehaves above ~100 Hz. Default stays 250 Hz. Installing this also updates the web pages.
RXV2-0.9.225-fc-telem-switch: New 'Flight controller on the telemetry line' switch on the Output protocol page. Untick it for plain CRSF-to-PWM servo converters: some echo junk that gets misread as telemetry (phantom current readings / false max-current alarms on the transmitter) — the receiver then ignores the telemetry line entirely and sends no Rotorflight probes. Default remains ON.
RXV2-0.9.226-async-update-check: The update check no longer blocks the receiver: manifest fetches now run in the background, so opening the app's front screen can't pause the servo output (the brief servo twitch with no transmitter connected). Results are cached for 10 minutes.
RXV2-0.9.227-vbat-adc: Receiver battery voltage on a spare pin: wire the pack through a 220k/10k divider (ratio 23.0, good to 12S; 100k/10k = 11.0 for 6S) + 100nF to D4 or D9 (free on 2-radio boards). Configure on the View-channels page; live volts (and per-cell if you set the cell count) shown there, and the voltage is sent to the transmitter as telemetry (12S pre-halve quirk handled).
RXV2-0.9.229-vbat-d9-only: Battery divider: D9 only (GPIO 8 — the one free pad on 2-radio boards; D4 carries the status LED), auto-detected when FC telemetry is off. IMPORTANT: replaces 0.9.227/228, which used wrong GPIO numbers for the divider pin (raw 9 = the SPI MOSI line!) — do not use those two versions with a divider.
RXV2-0.9.230-throttle-safe: SAFETY: the throttle channel (configurable on the Output protocol page, default 3) is held fully LOW (885 us) from power-on until the transmitter is actually heard — a receiver booted without its TX can no longer put the motor at half stick. Plus: booting with the TX already on now leaves Bluetooth open for 30 s (connect in that window and the link stays); and renaming the receiver from the app now works (inline rename box — the old popup was silently ignored by app WebViews).
RXV2-0.9.231-channels-tidy: Channel assignments consolidated: the arming channel now lives on the Output protocol page beside the throttle channel (one 'Channels' box); the arming card is gone from View channels. Battery card layout fixed so Pin/Ratio/Cells labels stay with their boxes on narrow phone screens.
RXV2-0.9.232-live-settings: Reboot only when it's actually needed: changing the CRSF rate, FC-telemetry switch, throttle channel or arming channel now applies instantly ('Saved — applied instantly' on the page, no reboot). Only changing the protocol itself (or PPM polarity) still reboots, because the output pin must be reconfigured.
RXV2-0.9.233-battery-save-dialog: Fixes the View-channels page broken in 0.9.231/232 (a script error meant Save battery settings did nothing and saved values weren't displayed — the settings themselves were never lost). Battery save now shows a proper 'Saved' confirmation dialog like the gear-ratio save.
RXV2-0.9.234-civilised-ota: Civilised OTA (Malcolm's word): when the connection drops during an install — routine over Bluetooth, and at the reboot moment on WiFi — the page no longer cries 'failed'. It says 'Installing… waiting for the receiver to come back', polls until the receiver reappears, and judges by the version it reports: new version = success (auto-reload), same old version = a real failure, still absent after 5 min = 'reload in a moment'.
RXV2-0.9.235-tx-failsafe: The transmitter's 'send failsafe to receiver' button now works on RXV2 (it was silently ignored): it captures the current channel positions — trims and subtrims included, since they're baked into the radio stream — exactly like the web 'Save failsafe' button. And with the FC-telemetry switch OFF (no flight controller, e.g. a PWM converter), the receiver now STREAMS the captured failsafe posture on CRSF after signal loss instead of going silent and letting the converter drift.
RXV2-0.9.236-install-clarity: Two update-flow niceties from Malcolm's hunting-lodge session: (1) trying to install while the receiver isn't on home WiFi now gets a plain explanation (the RECEIVER downloads the image itself, so the phone's internet can't help) instead of a cryptic failure; (2) an elapsed-time ticker during installs — the chip can't report true progress while flashing, but an honest count beats a frozen screen.
RXV2-0.9.237-bind-safe: SAFETY: the propeller could blip during a reboot-into-bind (prop fitted, hands near the model). Two defences: (1) every web-initiated reboot now pushes ~100ms of throttle-low frames and parks the output pin idle-high through the restart, so the converter/FC sees silence instead of noise; (2) the throttle stays pinned low until the link has delivered a stable stream (25 channel packets ≈ 0.5s) — covering the no-TX boot AND the first moments after binding, when a V1 transmitter in bind mode bypasses its own motor-low overrides.
RXV2-0.9.243-tidy-gaps-wave: Blackbox: TX switch-off no longer records a misleading final gap in saved flights. New: after the TX goes off, the receiver waves the ailerons when Bluetooth/WiFi become available.
RXV2-0.9.244-plane-blackbox: Blackbox now works on planes (no flight controller needed): flights record and save using the receiver's own battery divider. Adds radio swap count and per-transceiver time to flight stats. Includes the shutdown-gap trim and BLE aileron wave from 0.9.243.
RXV2-0.9.245-field-ble: Field mode is now Bluetooth-only (no more auto AP when home WiFi is absent; AP still available in WiFi settings). Update page explains the Bluetooth app path instead of claiming updates are impossible. Current-flight view no longer shows the TX switch-off as a scary longest gap. Flight graph: missing sensors greyed out, battery noise no longer magnified. Aileron wave now repeats on every landing of a session.
RXV2-0.9.246-ring-fix: Fixes the switch-off gap still showing (the trim ring was flooded by normal packets). Also skips the first seconds of battery sampling to kill a bogus 25V boot spike in the graph.
v0.9.265: Flights that never touch the arm switch (bench or simulated sessions) now save to flash via the link-dead fallback — Previous flights finally populate on receivers with an arming channel set.
v0.9.266: One-button polish: the No-transmitter-connected notice shows a single OK (OK and Cancel did the same thing).
v0.9.267: The no-transmitter notice now has exactly one button: Well of course!
v0.9.268: Saved flights are labelled with real date and time — the phone teaches the receiver the clock on every page visit, and flights saved before you connected are dated retroactively.
v0.9.269: Honest gap statistics: the receiver measures its own packet spacing (2 ms solo, 4 ms buddy-box) and counts only packets meaningfully LATE (default 5 ms or more, adjustable on the flight page) — and bills them only for the late part. The histogram now shows real anomalies, not every normal packet.
v0.9.270: Radio-swap count freezes at signal loss, exactly like the per-radio times — bench hunting while the transmitter is off is no longer billed to the flight.
v0.9.271: BLE quarantine for the black box: while a phone is connected over Bluetooth (or briefly around connect/disconnect), gaps and swaps are not billed to the RF link — the ESP32 BT radio desenses the nRF24s centimetres away, which never happens in real flight. Bench stats with the app attached now reflect the link, not the phone.
v0.9.272: Gap and swap statistics count ONLY when Bluetooth is fully off (fly mode) - nobody flies with Bluetooth on, so figures recorded with it running were never useful.
v0.9.273: Frame rate now reads the TRUE link rate from the measured packet spacing (matches the transmitter, ~500 Hz) instead of packets-divided-by-time; and a flight entered with the phone attached starts recording stats the moment the phone link drops.
v0.9.274: Fly now means true radio silence: the phone link is dropped too (it used to stay alive so fly mode could be cancelled from the app, but a live Bluetooth link desenses the RC radios). The way back is a power-cycle or landing auto-recovery.
v0.9.275: Three lodge-test refinements: the spacing estimator no longer lets missed-slot gaps inflate it (frame rate now agrees with the transmitter, ~500), transmitter power-off hesitations of ANY size are trimmed from the end of a flight record, and the post-Fly screen honestly says the Bluetooth link is closed instead of offering a button that cannot work.
v0.9.276: Frame rate tracks the true slot floor (retried packets no longer bias it - should now match the transmitter within a whisker) and the Bluetooth on/off quiet windows widen to 4 s so BT tail-end bursts cannot sneak one late packet into the record.
v0.9.277: Frame rate is now measured the V1 way: packets counted per second, exactly as the transmitter counts acknowledgements - the two ends finally use the same definition and must agree.
v0.9.278: Fly now zeroes the whole flight record 3 seconds later (Malcolm) - link stats AND the telemetry graph restart once the radios are truly quiet, so a flight begins at Fly, not at the bench.
v0.9.279: The battery guardian: at 3.5 V/cell the app shows a massive pulsing warning; at 3.3 V/cell - only if the channels have been dead-still for 2 minutes and the model is not armed or flying - the receiver saves the flight and deep-sleeps to spare the pack. A flying model always moves its channels, so sleep can never fire mid-air. Wake = power-cycle.
v0.9.280: Renaming the receiver over Bluetooth no longer strands you on a white page - the app shows a clear rebooting-as-NewName screen and tells you to reconnect from the scanner.
RXV2-0.9.281-exit-and-reload: After a rename the screen now says exactly what to do - exit and reload, the receiver reappears under its new name. Also fixed: the Android app was taking WiFi-flavoured wording everywhere (its Bluetooth disguise was not recognised).
RXV2-0.9.282-heli-wave: The Bluetooth-ready wave now shows on flight-controller models too (the disarmed FC passes cyclic to the swash, so you can see it) - with an extra guard: FC models only wave when no transmitter is live, so a mid-air reboot can never wiggle a flying machine.
RXV2-0.9.283-eight-flights: The black box now keeps the last EIGHT flights (was three) - a couple of bench tests can no longer push a real flight out of history. Updates still preserve all saved flights.
RXV2-0.9.284-flight-diary: The flight diary: keeps the last TWENTY flights; unarmed sessions under a minute are wiggle-checks and no longer saved at all; and updates now skip rewriting the web filesystem when it is unchanged (fingerprint match) - so saved flights survive every firmware-only update untouched and field updates get much faster. Background photo slimmed to make room.
RXV2-0.9.285-graph-scales: Flight-page polish from field review: the graph gains quarter-height gridlines and per-minute time marks (each trace still auto-scales to its own min-max shown in the key); the page title no longer hides behind the corner buttons; and a radio handover is now correctly billed to the flight (a 9-minute flight showed both radios busy yet zero swaps) - unbilled swaps leave a note in the events log saying why.
RXV2-0.9.286-landscape-graph: Turn the phone sideways on the flight page and the graph grows to fill most of the screen - landscape is reading mode, with a crisp high-resolution redraw on every rotation.
RXV2-0.9.287-y-scale: In landscape, every gridline now carries the actual VALUES - one number per trace, printed in that traces colour (each line has its own scale, so read the number that matches the colour). Also the corner buttons no longer sit on top of the cards in landscape.
RXV2-0.9.288-save-stall-quiet: Malcolm caught the receiver blaming the air for its own housekeeping: saving the flight at disarm stalls the loop (~1s with the 20-slot rotation) and an 808ms gap was billed exactly at arming-off. Saves now announce themselves and the statistics look away - self-inflicted stalls are never recorded as link quality.
RXV2-0.9.289-quiet-moment-save: Landing no longer makes the transmitter blink: the flight save now writes ONE ring slot instead of shuffling twenty files, and it waits for a provably quiet moment - disarmed with sticks still for two seconds (or transmitter off). A pilot flying an autorotation is never hands-still, so the save can never stall the link mid-air.
RXV2-0.9.290-ten-ms-doctrine: The 10ms doctrine: flight saves now trickle out a few hundred bytes per loop pass - no single pause the transmitter can even see (it logged the old save as a 250ms gap the receiver politely did not). And when WiFi is off with no phone attached and the link has been live 30 seconds, Bluetooth switches off too - nobody flies with Bluetooth on; it returns by itself after landing.
RXV2-0.9.291-flight-eraser: The flight diary gains an eraser: a Delete button appears when viewing any saved flight (never the live one) - tap twice to confirm, and a brief boring test vanishes to free its slot.
RXV2-0.9.292-govcfg-tracer: Detective work: the transmitter's global governor screen stays blank while the phone reads the same settings fine. This build adds breadcrumbs to the events log at every step of that path - open the screen on the transmitter once, and the log will point at the guilty stage.
RXV2-0.9.293-no-zero-latch: Case closed: the transmitter's global governor screen showed zeros because the receiver kept broadcasting empty parameter slots while the transmitter's request was still in flight - the screen latched the zeros and stopped listening a tenth of a second before the real values arrived. Now, like V1, those slots stay silent unless there is genuinely something to say.
RXV2-0.9.294-verified-writes: Trust, but verify: saving settings from the transmitter used to fire commands at the flight controller and hope - and on a busy wire the crucial save-to-memory command could vanish, quietly reverting your edit.
